items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: So you know it was a tremendous, tremendous band mainly because of the director and the inspiration. So he really inspired me.

ctx.x: My evolution into the tuba is that when I was very young, in elementary school they started a band program in my elementary school. And I brought the notice home to my mother and she was very excited. And so she signed me up for it, and I started, you know, so in those days you started as a class. You started as a band class. I started in the band class where you have clarinets, trumpets, trombones and everything in the class. Everybody learned at the same time. It’s not like I went out for a private instruction…

instrument: bassoons, trombones, trumpets, tubas you name it. Full clarinet section. And he played trumpet himself and then every day he’d have the band play [scats]. And the way he got us to want to do that is one of the first lessons he did, he would just take out the trumpet. He went [scats]. And that sounded so good that everybody wanted to be able to do it. So every rehearsal we’d start, right through the keys. He would have a different key. So we’d go like through all twelve keys. By the end of the year we…
You were like one on a part, too.
